name: L2 objective and gradient scaling
test:
import numpy as np
r=L2Regularizer(0.25)
w=np.array([2.,-3.])
assert np.isclose(r.loss_penalty(w),3.25)
assert np.allclose(r.gradiate_penalty(w),[1.,-1.5])
assert np.allclose(w,[2.,-3.])

name: Injected regularizer affects updates and epoch objective
input: custom regularizer, full batch, one epoch
test:
import numpy as np
class Custom(Regularizer):
    def gradiate_penalty(self,w): return np.array([0.75])
    def loss_penalty(self,w): return 2.5
x=np.array([[1.],[2.]])
y=np.array([0.,1.])
w,losses=train_logistic(x,y,Custom(),epochs=1,learning_rate=0.2,batch_size=2)
assert np.allclose(w,[-0.1])
z=x@w
expected=np.mean(np.logaddexp(0.,z)-y*z)+2.5
assert np.allclose(losses,[expected])

name: Zero regularization preserves baseline and inputs
input: two epochs with a final partial batch
test:
import numpy as np
x=np.array([[1.,2.],[-1.,3.],[2.,1.]])
y=np.array([1.,0.,1.])
old_x=x.copy();old_y=y.copy()
a=train_logistic(x,y,None,epochs=2,batch_size=2,seed=7)
b=train_logistic(x,y,L2Regularizer(0),epochs=2,batch_size=2,seed=7)
assert np.allclose(a[0],b[0]) and np.allclose(a[1],b[1])
assert len(a[1])==2 and np.isfinite(a[1]).all()
assert np.array_equal(x,old_x) and np.array_equal(y,old_y)

name: Penalty is applied at current weights without batch scaling
input: two full-batch steps with known gradient
test:
import numpy as np
x=np.array([[1.],[2.],[3.]])
y=np.array([0.,1.,1.])
r=L2Regularizer(0.3)
w,losses=train_logistic(x,y,r,epochs=2,learning_rate=0.1,batch_size=3)
first=np.array([0.2/3])
p=np.exp(-np.logaddexp(0.,-(x@first)))
expected=first-0.1*(x.T@(p-y)/3+0.6*first)
assert np.allclose(w,expected)
assert len(losses)==2

name: Final partial minibatch contributes an update
input: three identical samples, batch size two
test:
import numpy as np
x=np.ones((3,1)); y=np.ones(3)
w,_=train_logistic(x,y,None,epochs=1,learning_rate=0.2,batch_size=2)
first=0.1
expected=first-0.2*(1/(1+np.exp(-first))-1)
assert np.allclose(w,[expected])
